- If sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, reduce forecast slope; price tends to correct downward.  
- If forecast shows strong upward trend after a spike, cap the slope to avoid overshoot; sentiment decay often precedes reversal.  
- If true price deviates sharply from forecast early in horizon, assume mean reversion; adjust later days downward if sentiment turns negative.  
- If sentiment shows early positive spikes but price drops sharply, model may overestimate momentum — reduce forecast amplitude.  
- For 30-day horizons, if forecast is >90% of recent 7-day high, flag for overconfidence; sentiment decay may signal correction.  
- If sentiment is positive but price falls below forecast, model may be ignoring sentiment signal — adjust downward by 5–10% of forecast gap.
